newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bayrou calls for centre-right overhaul.
newsitem.headline: France's Bayrou calls for centre-right overhaul.

text.p: French centrist leader Francois Bayrou called on Monday for a deep reorganisation of the defeated centre-right in order to let all its political components find a role.

Bayrou, the outgoing education minister, said the way the centre-right was organised had prevented political trends like the authoritarian right, free marketeers and social centrists from making their point to voters.

"Because of the architecture of the coalition, voices in the right and the centre are being cut off. We must re-think the architecture so that these necessary and indispensable voices be heard," he told France Inter radio.
The defeated coalition is made up of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) and the Union for French Democracy umbrella group.

Bayrou, who heads Democratic Force, one of the main UDF components, said he did not mean founding a new party but wanted a reorganisation in order to boost the centre to prepare for another possible snap election.
"The centre is powerful in public opinion, but could not express itself and build itself," he said.
"We have a duty to build in order to attract the largest number of French people, including from the left and those who voted for the far right although they are not far righists," he said.

The right erupted into bitter bickering on Sunday night after its resounding election defeat at the hands of the left and several of its rival leaders thrust themselves forward to lead the reconstruction.
As well as Bayrou, Gaullists Philippe Seguin, ex-premier Edouard Balladur and hardliner Charles Pasqua were among senior politicians who called for a profound overhaul of the conservative coalition.
